If I have been overzealous as of late, it’s only because I care about this community and hate to see it degenerate into an echo chamber of negativity, political sniping, and inconsideration. I’ve never been shy about sharing my job as a pediatrician, my proud work for Cincinnati Children’s Hospital, and my identity for those who have asked. Just relieved I didn't have to the first (or 10th) person to point out that this isn't what "infinite scroll" is, at all. I get playing a little fast and loose with the terminology – it's a crossword, not a Ux design textbook – but this is one particularly brutal. 

Would you loop elements on a carousel? Absolutely. It's implied in the name. But having an infinite scroll just Pac-Mac content back into view would be patently insane. Any self-respecting engineer would stop the feature this puzzle describes from ever being built, because it's the sort of thing that would have to be rolled back instantly, after every user who encountered it reported it as a bug.

Oh, brilliant concept!:

Let the first 12 down answers be unclued, which leaves the first ten across answers uncrossed, which starts the solver out in the hole.  To give the solver “the thing with feathers”, the middle section is clued relatively easy, uncovering the revealer.  Then, at the bottom, finally, the solver thrillingly sees the gimmick, and the puzzle quickly falls in a swoop.

Brilliant.  Plaudits to the brain that came up with this, not to mention, that duplicated in the box the feeling you get online during an infinite scroll, where suddenly the bottom of a page becomes the top of a new one.  Wow!

And plaudits to the technician that executed it, that had to not only connect those bottom down answers to those on top, but have all the answers -- across and down -- be real words!

For me, an amazing journey from “Wha?” to “Hah!”  I shake my head slowly in wonder at what can be done in the crossword box.

Thank you, Enrique, for a sublime journey today.  Bravo, sir!
